propositions: The epic-close bug screen converts systematic LLM provider errors into per-candidate 'unrelated' (C) verdicts, silently degrading the caused_by bug floor to a no-op with no aggregate signal.
max_tokens is never re-clamped when a model shrinks during structured_run execution, causing Bedrock to reject requests exceeding the resolved model's 64K ceiling with a 400 error.

LLMUnavailableError (including subclass LLMConfigError) raised from the epic-close bug screen must propagate and block the close instead of degrading, consistent with the absent-provider fail-closed path.
Non-provider per-candidate screen failures must continue to degrade to C ('unrelated') to preserve the intended advisory-screen behavior.
--force-close must remain a valid escape hatch to bypass completion verification when an LLM provider is unavailable or misconfigured.
